A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FinRAGBench-V and RGenCite. Their main text, equations, results, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison after matching relocated material.

before.justification: V1 reports original retrieval, generation, and visual-citation experiments in Tables 4–6, supplemented by task-wise results and error cases.

after.justification: V2 retains the original benchmark experiments, citation-evaluation correlations, task-wise results, and error analyses.

M1.justification: RGenCite retains the same retrieval and joint answer/citation generation procedure, coordinate-based citations, and generation prompt. Neither citation-evaluation approach changes.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same Chinese and English financial corpus and 1,394 QA pairs across seven question categories. Document sources, modalities, and single-page/multi-page coverage remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Tables 4–6 retain the same nine retrievers, thirteen generation models, and citation-evaluator configurations. Added model citations do not introduce additional evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Top-10 retrieval, Marker text extraction, answer metrics, citation metrics, and human-evaluation procedures remain unchanged. The added QA-verification guideline documents existing curation rather than reporting a revised experimental protocol.

E4.justification: The task-wise comparison in Figure 5, evaluation-method analysis in Table 6, and Appendix E error cases are retained. Relocation does not introduce new analyses.

E5.justification: Both report the same Pearson, Spearman, and Kendall correlations. Neither introduces repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or other uncertainty-reporting changes.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 4–6 and Figure 5 match. The appendix examples and error-case findings also remain unchanged; no new performance results are reported.

T1.justification: The task definitions, citation-coordinate representation, and recall, irrelevance, and precision definitions in Equations 1–3 are unchanged. Neither version contains additional theoretical proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same benchmark, RGenCite baseline, automatic citation-evaluation contribution, and claims about current model limitations.

C2.justification: Interpretations of retrieval superiority, reasoning difficulties, and block-level citation weaknesses remain unchanged. The dedicated-model limitation and Appendix H discussion of data noise, annotation errors, and generalizability are retained.

D1.justification: V2 adds dataset and code links on the first page. Appendix F/Table 27 expands QA-verification instructions with explicit retain/revise/discard rules. Existing prompts, hardware, API costs, and annotator counts remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds seven references for already-used model families while retaining the related-work arguments and novelty positioning. Some model/reference versions differ: Gemini-2.0-Flash cites a report titled Gemini 2.5.

P1.justification: V2 updates author/contact information, adds acknowledgements, reorganizes the annotation and resource appendices, and updates cross-references. The main exposition and existing appendix prose remain largely verbatim.

P2.justification: V2 resizes several displays, including Tables 1 and 6, adjusts Figure 1, and relocates figures and appendix material. It adds QA-guideline Table 27; the existing citation-rating guideline becomes Table 28.

improvement.justification: The new resource links and explicit QA-verification guideline improve usability and curation transparency, while larger displays improve readability. These are limited gains because the scientific evidence is unchanged. The added model-reference version mismatches slightly weaken citation precision but do not outweigh the documentation improvements.
